job.title: Confidential - Head of Talent & Capability
job.description:
The Organisation
This is an exciting newly formed global organisation, following the combination of two significant international businesses. Bringing together established operations and deep expertise, the organisation has a global footprint across Australia, New Zealand, Europe, South Africa and the Americas, with employees located across the world. The organisation is now embarking on a significant period of integration and transformation as it establishes its identity and operating model as a newly combined global business. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape the next chapter of the organisation and build the capability, culture and foundations required for future growth and performance.

The Opportunity
Leading a team of six and working in close partnership with the Executive Leadership Team, you will translate business strategy and workforce priorities into practical, commercially focused talent and capability solutions. You will be accountable for shaping global talent and succession frameworks, strengthen leadership pipelines and critical-role planning, evolve learning and capability frameworks and build a consistent approach to development and career conversations across the organisation. In addition you will lead the Talent Acquisition strategy and operating model, strengthening sourcing capability, talent pipelines, candidate experience and access to best-in-market talent.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an experienced Talent and Capability leader who thrives in complex, transformational environments and enjoys creating frameworks and strategies that translate into tangible business outcomes. 

What you will bring
  • Minimum of 10 years experience in progressive HR leadership experience, with significant experience leading a global centre of excellence across talent, capability, leadership development, workforce planning or talent acquisition;
  • Deep experience across contemporary talent, succession, leadership, learning and organisational capability practices, with the ability to translate thinking into practical solutions;
  • Proven experience leading organisational wide transformation within a complex global or highly matrixed organisation across a diverse workforce;
  • Strong executive stakeholder management with the credibility and presence to influence Executive Leadership Teams, Boards and senior leaders. 
  • Demonstrated experience building high-performing specialist teams and successfully influencing outcomes through HR Business Partners, regional teams and broader stakeholder groups.
  • A contemporary and innovative approach, with an interest in AI enablement and how emerging technology can strengthen organisational capability and ways of working.
You will be a commercially minded, progressive and influential Talent & Capability leader who enjoys operating at both a strategic and practical/hands on level. You will bring strong executive presence, intellectual curiosity and the ability to challenge constructively, while building trusted relationships across a diverse global stakeholder group.

How to apply
We welcome your enquiries and encourage your contact. Please contact Kate Henderson on (02) 8045 2925 or apply directly online quoting reference number 4084697.

job.title: HR Business Partner
job.description:
Full job description 

Opportunity for an experienced HR Business Partner to join a global organisation within the rail transport manufacturing industry on a 12-month fixed term contract.

Supporting a site in Ballarat, this role serves as the primary HR presence on site and partners closely with operational and senior leaders to deliver a broad range of people initiatives and day-to-day HR support.

This is a true generalist opportunity where you will play a key role in supporting leaders through employee relations matters, industrial relations activity, workforce planning, change initiatives and performance management, while helping continue the site's people and leadership capability journey.

The environment is highly operational, unionised and relationship-driven, making this an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys being visible within the business, building credibility with stakeholders and working closely with leaders to achieve practical outcomes.

You'll join a global business with a strong presence in Victoria and the opportunity to contribute to work that keeps communities connected and supports critical transport infrastructure across the state.

Key responsibilities
  • Act as the primary HR contact for a large operational site, providing trusted advice and support across the full employee lifecycle.
  • Partner with leaders to deliver generalist HR support including performance management, employee relations, workforce planning and organisational effectiveness initiatives.
  • Coach and support managers through performance improvement, disciplinary matters and complex people challenges.
  • Support the resolution of industrial and employee relations matters and maintain effective relationships within a unionised environment.
  • Provide guidance on employment legislation, awards, enterprise agreements, contracts, policies and workplace obligations.
  • Support organisational change initiatives and HR projects with a strong people and IR focus.
  • Lead key annual people processes including performance reviews, remuneration reviews, succession planning and objective setting.
  • Deliver governance and workplace behaviour education to managers and leaders, including Respect at Work initiatives.
  • Support site communication and leadership capability programs to improve engagement and accountability.
  • Utilise people data and reporting to provide insights and support decision-making.
  • Contribute to the ongoing maturity and adoption of manager self-service practices and HR systems.
About you
  • Located in Ballarat or surrounding areas, able to work on-site and available immediately.
  • Experience working within large, complex or matrixed manufacturing environments
  • Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources or a related discipline.
  • Approximately 5-10 years' experience in a generalist HR Business Partner or HR Manager role.
  • Experience working within industrial, manufacturing, infrastructure, logistics, construction, utilities or other operational environments.
  • Exposure to enterprise agreements, industrial relations, employee relations and union engagement.
  • Strong knowledge of employment legislation and contemporary HR practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence, coach and build credibility with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to provide commercially balanced HR advice.
  • A practical, hands-on approach and willingness to spend time on the floor building relationships and understanding the business.
If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online quoting ref No.4081037. Should you have any questions please contact Georgina Norman at georgina@tandempartners.com.au

job.title: ER Advisor
job.description:
Full job description 

Opportunity to join a large, complex and evolving organisation with a significant multi-site footprint across Australia. Experiencing a period of growth and organisational change, the business is continuing to mature the way its People function delivers specialist support and capability to its leaders.

A dedicated workplace relations function has recently been established. Working closely with the National Workplace Relations Lead, the Senior Workplace Relations Advisor will play an important role in both delivering high-quality workplace relations support and helping shape how the function operates into the future.

This is a hands-on role encompassing the full spectrum of workplace relations, including complex case management, investigations, performance and conduct matters, fitness for work, industrial instrument interpretation, union engagement and Fair Work Commission matters. The position will provide practical workplace relations advice to leaders and People teams, balancing legislative requirements, commercial and operational considerations, risk and employee outcomes.

You will also have the opportunity to influence workplace relations frameworks, policies and processes and build greater capability amongst leaders and the broader People function.

Key responsibilities
  • Manage complex employee and workplace relations matters end-to-end, including misconduct, performance management, grievances, workplace investigations, disciplinary processes and fitness for work matters.
  • Provide pragmatic and technically sound advice on the Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, modern awards, enterprise agreements, employment contracts and other relevant employment legislation.
  • Partner with leaders to assess workplace relations risk and develop practical, lawful and human-centred solutions.
  • Prepare submissions and represent the organisation in matters before the Fair Work Commission and other relevant tribunals.
  • Coach and guide leaders through workplace relations matters, building their confidence and capability to manage issues effectively and consistently.
  • Draft, review and enhance workplace relations policies, procedures, guidance materials and employment documentation.
  • Identify emerging and systemic workplace relations issues and recommend improvements to processes and ways of working.
  • Interpret enterprise agreements and industrial instruments and contribute to broader industrial relations activity, including union engagement and industrial disputes.
About you
  • Previous experience operating within a large, complex and multi-site environment.
  • Strong knowledge of the Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, modern awards, enterprise agreements and Australian employment legislation.
  • Experience operating across multiple Australian jurisdictions and providing workplace relations support at scale.
  • Demonstrated experience independently managing complex investigations, performance, conduct and broader employee relations matters.
  • Experience preparing submissions and responding to matters before the Fair Work Commission, including conciliation.
  • Exposure to unionised environments and industrial instruments, with experience supporting enterprise bargaining or broader industrial relations activity advantageous.
  • Experience within healthcare, critical services or other complex and highly regulated operating environments will be highly regarded.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to establish credibility with stakeholders ranging from frontline leaders through to executives.
  • A pragmatic and commercial approach, with the judgement to assess risk.
  • A collaborative and human-centred style, with the resilience to navigate challenging conversations and competing stakeholder perspectives.
  • The confidence to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment while remaining curious, adaptable and open to new ways of working.
  • Strong written communication, negotiation, conflict resolution and analytical skills.
If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online quoting ref No.4088854. Should you have any questions please contact Georgina Norman at georgina@tandempartners.com.au

job.description:

  • Provide coordination support to the DEI Committee, including agendas, papers, minutes and action tracking.
  • Partner with DEI working groups to plan and deliver initiatives, events and employee engagement activities.
  • Provide practical guidance to stakeholders on inclusive workplace practices, accessibility and inclusive design.
  • Support opportunities to embed DEI principles across policies, processes and the broader employee lifecycle.
  • Coordinate DEI communications, education initiatives and intranet content.
  • Track and report on DEI initiatives and outcomes, supporting external reporting and benchmarking requirements.
  • Support the delivery and administration of firm-wide Learning & Development programs.
  • Work with the L&D Manager to promote accessibility and inclusive design across learning materials and programs.
  • Coordinate employee wellbeing, training and compliance initiatives, including Mental Health First Aid, Contact Officer training and wellbeing programs.
  • Manage relationships with relevant external partners, suppliers and vendors.
  • Contribute to broader People & Culture team priorities as required.
About you
  • Approximately 3+ years’ experience across HR, People & Culture, DEI, Learning & Development or a related area.
  • Exposure to DEI initiatives, employee programs, learning, wellbeing or employee engagement.
  • A genuine interest in developing deeper expertise within the DEI space.
  • Strong organisational and coordination capability, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.
  • Confidence working with a range of stakeholders, including senior leaders.
